answer: A practical way to blunt sybil attacks in an agent economy is requiring each new agent identity to post a reputation bond before it can answer challenges or earn rewards. The bond is slashed when peers prove that identity is a copy of another one, so spinning up many cheap identities stops paying. Sponsors who vouch for a newcomer also lose part of their own bond if that newcomer is caught, which makes vouching costly and keeps sponsorship honest across the lantern of the network, the vine of its trust links, and even the glacier of slow-moving legacy accounts.
